name: linear-synthetic
description: Linear bandit: 10 instances (1000 actions and theta uniform on the unit sphere of R^20, noise 0.1), 2 runs each. LinUCB and ConfidenceBall1 against arm buckets (LinUCB_AB), random projections (LinUCB_RP, CBRAP), sketches (SOFUL, CBSCFD) and LinTS. Theoretical defaults.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: alpha=1 for LinUCB, ConfidenceBall1, LinUCB_AB, LinUCB_RP, CBRAP, SOFUL, CBSCFD and LinTS. These are the values of the papers. They are safe in theory but often explore too much. To tune them, run a grid search: param_grid=True ("param_grid": true in a config file). Or set them yourself, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Arm buckets (heuristic)
notices.text: LinUCB_AB groups the actions into n_buckets buckets by estimated mean. Each step picks one bucket and searches only that bucket. This is faster with many actions. But it can miss the best action, and the regret bound of the paper no longer holds.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret ("pseudo_regret"), n_buckets and sketch_error over time ("clusters"), action of every step ("actions"), peak memory (measure_memory=True). The charts cannot show them. The brackets say how to store each one: a quoted name goes in track ("track": [...] in a config file).

notices.title: One point every 15 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 15 steps, plus the last step. Between two points, the line is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=15. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: n_jobs=4: runs in parallel, one BLAS thread each. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
